Definition: Where multimodal fusion occurs in the pipeline.
Allowed Values / Coding Rule: F0 No fusion; F1 Input/data-level; F2 Representation-level; F3 Deep/token-level interactive; F4 Decision-level; F5 Hybrid/multi-stage
Example / Note: Code the dominant demonstrated fusion stage; use F5 only when multiple fusion stages are explicitly combined.

Definition: Mechanism used to combine or align modalities.
Allowed Values / Coding Rule: Concatenation; Linear projection; MLP; Cross-attention; Bidirectional cross-attention; Q-Former/query tokens; Gated fusion; Attention weighting; MoE; Graph fusion; Tensor/bilinear fusion; Textual transformation; Decision ensemble; Other; NR
Example / Note: Multiple values may be entered separated by semicolons.

Definition: Granularity at which cross-modal information is integrated.
Allowed Values / Coding Rule: G1 Global; G2 Region-level; G3 Patch/token-level; G4 Concept-level; G5 Patient-level; G6 Longitudinal; G7 Multi-granular
Example / Note: Use G7 when the study explicitly combines two or more granularities.
Text queries image features = unidirectional; image↔text interaction = bidirectional.

Definition: Whether information is fused across time.
Example / Note: Longitudinal requires multiple time points or encounters.

Allowed Values / Coding Rule: P0 Population-level; P1 Static patient context; P2 Multimodal patient contextualization; P3 Longitudinal personalization; P4 Adaptive patient-specific reasoning; P5 Clinically validated personalized decision support
Example / Note: Assign conservatively from demonstrated methods/evidence, not authors' claims.

Definition: Retrieval strategy used at inference or reasoning time.
Allowed Values / Coding Rule: None; Static external context; RAG; Hybrid RAG; Graph-RAG; Multimodal RAG; Patient-specific RAG; Multi-round RAG; Agentic retrieval; Other; NR
Example / Note: Generic RAG is not automatically patient-specific RAG.

Definition: Explicit mechanism used to structure or improve reasoning.
Allowed Values / Coding Rule: None explicitly; Prompted CoT; Supervised reasoning; Self-consistency; Self-reflection; Verification; RL-based reasoning; Tool-augmented reasoning; Agentic reasoning; Multi-agent; Other; NR
Example / Note: Record only what is actually implemented/evaluated.

Definition: Strength of evidence supporting a safety/risk mitigation claim.
Allowed Values / Coding Rule: R0 Not investigated; R1 Proposed only; R2 Qualitative evidence; R3 Quantitative benchmark evidence; R4 External/clinical evidence; R5 Prospective/workflow evidence
Example / Note: The level reflects evidence strength, not novelty.

Definition: Maturity of evidence from benchmark testing to clinical translation.
Allowed Values / Coding Rule: T0 Benchmark only; T1 Retrospective clinical evaluation; T2 Generalizability evaluation; T3 Prospective clinical evaluation; T4 Workflow impact; T5 Clinical outcome/regulatory evidence
Example / Note: Clinician review is captured separately and does not automatically raise T-level.

Definition: Whether multimodal-vs-unimodal results are scientifically comparable.
Example / Note: Yes only if dataset, split, task, metric, and evaluation protocol are directly comparable.

Definition: Performance gain attributable to fusion when eligible.
Allowed Values / Coding Rule: Numeric; leave blank when not eligible
Example / Note: Higher-is-better: multimodal − strongest unimodal. Lower-is-better: strongest unimodal − multimodal.

Definition: Reviewer confidence in the extracted/coded value.
Example / Note: Use Low when architecture or evaluation details are ambiguous.

Definition: Where the coded evidence appears in the source paper.
Example / Note: Example: Methods §3.2; Fig. 2; Table 4; Supplementary Table S3.
Use NR instead of guessing or inferring missing details.
